display.title: Grape Town: The King's Barrel of Wine
display.summary_short: A boy wonders whether he must daven if the whole class is davening anyway. His teacher answers with the story of a town that filled the king's barrel with wine, or so everyone thought.
display.summary_long: In class, a boy's yetzer hara argues that he need not say every word of davening, since the whole class is davening and Moshiach will come anyway; his yetzer tov answers that the Rebbe said each person must do his own part. After davening the teacher tells a story. Grape Town grows the sweetest grapes in the land, and its people make the finest wine. When the king announces a royal visit to taste it, everyone wants the honor of serving him, so they agree to pour a bottle each into one giant barrel in the marketplace. Along the way the storyteller explains why wine must be kept covered from non-Jews and what mevushal wine is. Beryl climbs the ladder with his best wine, then decides to keep it and pour in water instead, since no one will notice one bottle. But every single townsperson has the same idea. When the king opens the tap, out comes water, again and again. The king is not angry: he teaches them to do good things themselves and not rely on others. The boy understands, and from then on davens every word, because Hashem wants to hear every child's voice.
display.lesson: When there is something good to do, do it yourself and don't rely on others; Hashem wants to hear every child's own davening.

characters: his yetzer tov and yetzer hara
